newsitem.title: MEXICO: Cemex Q3 results surprisingly good.
newsitem.headline: Cemex Q3 results surprisingly good.

text.p: Third-quarter results for cement giant Cemex SA were a pleasant surprise, above all because of greater profitability in its Mexico unit, analysts said.
"In Mexico, the results were slightly better than expected, and in the international operation slightly below expectations," said analyst Eric Linder of J.P. Morgan.
Analysts said they were focusing on Cemex's operating income rather than net profit, which was distorted by foreign exchange and monetary losses.

Cemex's operating income was 2.776 billion pesos for the first nine months, up from 2.653 billion for the same period in 1995, while net profit was 5.611 billion pesos for nine months, down sharply from 7.054 billion pesos in 1995.

Earnings per share were 0.92 pesos in the third quarter, somewhat below a forecast of 1.03 pesos based on a Reuters survey of six analysts. "You have to look at the increase in (sales) volumes in Mexico compared to the third quarter of 1995 (up 17 percent) which turned out better than I expected," Linder said. "For the fourth quarter, I don't see any important fall in the tonnage in Mexico."
Linder estimated that Cemex's market share rose about three percentage points to 60 percent as rival Apasco SA de CV saw sales volumes remain flat in the third quarter.

"Cemex reported margins that were very good (31 percent in the third quarter) and recovered market share, all while being able to increase prices," said Carmen Slade, an analyst with Salomon Brothers. "Nonetheless, their international units didn't do as well as Mexico."
However, UBS Securities analyst Alvaro Shiraishi noted that Cemex's Colombian operation did particularly well.
"Colombia validated Cemex's strategy of making acquisitions," Shiraishi said. "Colombia effectively raised the value of the company."
Still, analysts are not expecting the fourth quarter to be as strong as the third.

"The volumes in Mexico in the fourth quarter aren't going to be as aggressive," said Paul Rodriguez of Caspian Securities. "Cemex is revising its estimate for national growth that will be around zero to one percent in 1996 over 1995."
Analysts also said a price war was looming.
